questions.question: A developer accepts a GitHub Copilot suggestion that calls a method named formatCurrencySafe(). The method does not exist in the project or in any installed package. Which limitation of generative AI does this illustrate?

options.text: Hallucination
options.why: Correct. The model produced a plausible but non-existent method based on patterns, not on the project's code.

options.text: Knowledge cut-off
options.why: A knowledge cut-off explains unawareness of recent changes. The method never existed, so this is not the best match.

options.text: Non-deterministic output
options.why: Non-determinism means different results for the same prompt. It does not explain an invented method.

options.text: Public code matching
options.why: Public code matching concerns suggestions that resemble public repositories. It does not describe an invented API.

questions.explanation: A hallucination is output that appears correct but is fabricated, such as a function, package or setting that does not exist.

questions.question: A team notices that GitHub Copilot suggests an older version of a library and does not use an API that was released recently. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The model's training data has a knowledge cut-off date
options.why: Correct. Releases after the training data ends may be unknown to the model, so older patterns are suggested.

options.text: Content exclusions are blocking the library's documentation
options.why: Content exclusions apply to files in your repositories, not to the model's knowledge of public libraries.

options.text: The public code filter is set to Block
options.why: The filter hides suggestions that match public code. It does not cause outdated versions to be suggested.

options.text: The developer does not have a Copilot seat
options.why: Without access the developer would receive no suggestions at all.

questions.explanation: Large language models learn from data up to a cut-off date, so suggestions can be outdated. Validate versions against current documentation.

questions.question: Two developers enter the same prompt in GitHub Copilot Chat and receive different implementations of the same function. Which statement explains this behavior?

options.text: Generative AI output is non-deterministic, so the same prompt can produce different results
options.why: Correct. Generation involves sampling, so responses can vary between runs.

options.text: One of the developers has an outdated extension that returns cached answers
options.why: Copilot does not return cached answers from an outdated extension. Variation is expected behavior.

options.text: Copilot executes both versions and returns whichever runs faster
options.why: Copilot does not execute code to choose a response.

options.text: The organization policy randomly assigns a different model to each user
options.why: Organizations control which models are allowed, but varying output for the same prompt is a property of generation itself.

questions.explanation: Because outputs vary, a single answer should not be treated as authoritative. Tests decide whether a version is correct.

questions.question: Which TWO statements accurately describe limitations of the large language models used by GitHub Copilot?

options.text: The model can only consider the content that fits within its limited context window
options.why: Correct. Code outside the prompt is not visible to the model.

options.text: The model may generate code that contains security vulnerabilities
options.why: Correct. Insecure patterns exist in training data and can appear in suggestions.

options.text: The model runs unit tests on each suggestion before displaying it
options.why: Copilot does not execute or test code before suggesting it.

options.text: The model always produces better results for rare programming languages
options.why: Suggestions are typically weaker for languages with less training data.

questions.explanation: LLMs have a limited context window and can produce insecure code. They do not run code and perform less well on rarely used languages.

questions.question: A developer asks GitHub Copilot Chat to rewrite a 5,000-line legacy file in one request. Copilot's version omits several business rules that appear near the end of the file. What should the developer do to reduce this risk?

options.text: Split the work into smaller functions, add tests for the current behavior first, and review each change
options.why: Correct. Smaller requests fit in the context window, and tests confirm that behavior is preserved.

options.text: Repeat the same request until Copilot returns a version that includes every rule
options.why: Repeating the request does not address the context limit and provides no verification.

options.text: Disable the public code filter so that Copilot can use more context
options.why: The public code filter does not affect how much context Copilot can read.

options.text: Add the file to a content exclusion list
options.why: Excluding the file would stop Copilot from using it as context at all.

questions.explanation: The limited context window can cause Copilot to miss content in large inputs. Breaking the task down and testing existing behavior mitigates this.
